title: Signal isolation and dead-metric recovery - oncall scratchpad
body:
Executive summary:
We observed repeated SLO burn alerts over a 48h window driven by a combination of (a) periodic exporter restarts on a subset of services, (b) a metrics exporter that started returning 503s for ~10-15m, and (c) an aggressive burn-rate alert that amplifies short-lived gaps into high-priority pages. This doc captures the oncall investigation, temporary mitigations we used to quiet the blast, and proposed durable fixes to avoid future false SLO escalations.

Symptoms seen:
- Multiple pagers triggered for "SLO token-generation Latency burn" between 2024-11-06 02:12 and 2024-11-07 09:00 UTC.
- Prometheus dashboards showed a sudden drop to zero in kvcache/cache_hit_ratio and exporter_up{job="token-exporter"} flipped to 0 in multiple clusters.
- alertmanager spam: identical alert fired across 6 alertmanager instances — duplicate deliveries due to missing dedupe labels.
- Oncall notes flagged an uptick in pager volume: ~27 pages in 3 hours vs baseline 2-3.

Immediate triage (what we did during incident):
- Signal isolation: muted the SLO burn alert policy for the affected route for 30 minutes instead of global mute. Reason: give breathing room while preserving coverage elsewhere.
- Silence duplicate deliveries by adding temporary alertmanager inhibition rule to drop identical alert fingerprints from noisy alertmanager endpoints.
- Verified exporters: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=token-exporter && kubectl -n monitoring logs <pod> --since=1h. Found recurring OOMKilled events on exporter pods in us-west-prod-1.
- Queried Prometheus to map missing-series pattern:  absent_over_time(up{job="token-exporter"}[20m]) and count by(cluster)(absent_over_time(kvcache_cache_hit_ratio{route=~".*token.*"}[10m]))
- Applied emergency restart to exporter daemonset after rolling back 1 recent config change (env var bump).

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Exporter OOMs triggered by a recent buffered-metrics change that increased in-memory metric cardinality (most likely). Evidence: pod OOM events + recent PR merged to telemetry repo (linked_artifacts).
2) A rate-limiting proxy intermittently returning 503s for /metrics endpoints, causing collectors to mark series as absent. Evidence: 503 spikes in proxy logs coincident with metric drop windows.
3) Alert configuration sensitivity: the SLO burn rule uses 5m window with exponential burn multiplier, so short 10–15m gaps produce large burn signals and pages.

Temporary mitigations (followups to ensure stability):
- Short-term: keep targeted silence on the SLO burn rule for affected routes until exporters are stable (not longer than 2 hours without postmortem). Document reason in silence with link to this doc.
- Add a 3-min cooldown in alertmanager routing for identical alertnames from same cluster to reduce duplicates while debugging.
- Roll back telemetry PR 214 in staging and promote a fixed patch that reduces label cardinality.

Runbook additions (proposed durable runbook changes):
- Discovery quick-check checklist (to run on first page):
  1) Check exporter health: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l job=token-exporter -o wide
  2) Check exporter logs for OOM/kernel OOM: kubectl describe pod <pod> and kubectl logs <pod> --previous
  3) Query Prometheus for absent series: absent_over_time(up{job="token-exporter"}[10m])
  4) Query for metric cardinality spike: increase(count by(__name__, job, route)(metrics[1h])[1h]) > threshold
  5) Check proxy 5xxs: kubectl -n ingress logs <proxy-pod> --since=30m | grep "/metrics"
- Recommended immediate thresholds: if >30% of exporter replicas show OOM in 1h, trigger SRE pager for telemetry team (separate from SLO burn).
- Add synthetic heartbeat metric: telemetry_exporter_heartbeat{job="token-exporter"} emitted every 1m with a low-cardinality label set (cluster, region). Use this for exporter liveness instead of relying solely on raw /metrics presence.
- Alert tuning: replace extreme burn-rate multiplier on short windows with a two-tiered approach:
  * fast-warning (non-pager) for 5m dips -> notify slack #sre-observability
  * slow-burn (pagerable) for sustained 30m+ SLO deviations
- Alertmanager dedupe: ensure external_labels include cluster and zone; add fingerprinting to alerts to avoid multi-delivery from multi-cluster federation.

Backfill and SLO accounting notes:
- For SLO fairness, we will mark the 10–15m windows caused by exporter OOMs as "service-impacting but telemetry missing" and request a one-off SLO adjustment using the SLO correction workflow (see linked_artifacts).
- Backfilling options: if prometheus remote_write contains recent samples, we can reconstruct availability using scraped samples; otherwise mark as unverifiable and submit for SLO forgiveness. Steps:
  1) Check remote_write buffer (loki/bigtable) for metric samples in that window.
  2) If present, run a reconciliation query to synthesize availability series and update the SLO calculator.

Experiment log (ideas to test):
- Adaptive quiet-window: apply a short, auto-expiring suppression if >50% of alerts of same fingerprint appear from a single cluster in <10m. Measure reduction in duplicate pages.
- Prefix caching: reduce exporter label cardinality by sharding labels into a static tag map rather than high-cardinality dynamic tags. Test in staging route token-generator-qa for 72h.
- Dynamic burn-rate smoothing: implement a smoothing filter in SLO pipeline that requires burn contribution to persist for 2 consecutive windows before pagers escalate.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Asha: complete postmortem draft w/ timeline & RCA by 2024-11-18.
- Ben: revert & patch telemetry PR 214 in staging and validate memory profile by 2024-11-12.
- Mariana: implement synthetic heartbeat metric and add to exporter library, PR by 2024-12-01.
- DevOps: add alertmanager inhibition rule template and safe-silence checklist into runbook by 2024-11-20.

Notes to future oncallers:
- Prefer targeted silences over global silences. Document the reason and expected duration.
- When observing a metric vanishing pattern, check both exporter pod state and any network path (proxy/sidecar) that sits between collector and exporter.
- If the SLO burn alert is noisy during telemetry recovery, avoid an immediate config flip of thresholds — instead use targeted silences and follow the runbook above.

Appendix - useful queries and commands:
- Missing exporter series: absent_over_time(up{job="token-exporter"}[15m])
- Count distinct exporters reporting: count(count_without(job, instance)(up{job="token-exporter"}))
- kvcache hit drop: increase(kvcache_cache_hit_ratio{route=~".*token.*"}[10m]) < 0.02
- Debugging exporter pods: kubectl -n monitoring describe pod <pod> | egrep -i "oom|killed|evicted"
- Check alertmanager silences: amtool silence query --active --label matcher=alertname="SLO Burn"

Raw oncall log excerpts (abbreviated):
- 2024-11-07 02:18 UTC - page received: SLO burn token-generation high (route: /v1/tokens)
- 2024-11-07 02:22 UTC - Asha: queried prometheus -> absent over time showed 4/6 exporters missing
- 2024-11-07 02:27 UTC - Ben: found OOMKilled on exporter pod  token-exporter-2; rolled restart after rollback env var
- 2024-11-07 03:05 UTC - Mariana: applied short mute on SLO alert for route /v1/tokens (30m)
- 2024-11-07 03:40 UTC - pages subsided; monitoring shows exporters stable; began follow-ups

Open questions:
- Can the telemetry library enforce low-cardinality labels at compile time? (devs: Mariana + telemetry team)
- Should SLO burn calculation ignore windows where telemetry_exporter_heartbeat is absent? pros/cons?
- Is there a way to make alertmanager federation not duplicate deliveries without risking missed cross-cluster alerts?

If you're reading this during oncall: add your steps and local findings below, then file a linked postmortem when the incident is over.

-- Asha K.
